questions.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is orthogonal.
questions.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}},$ $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}},$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{3}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{1\cdot (-1)+4\cdot 1+3\cdot 1+1\cdot 1}{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{1}=\frac{7}{4}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{1\cdot 3+4\cdot 1+3\cdot 1+1\cdot 1}{{3}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{11}{12}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{3}}{{a}_{3}\cdot {a}_{3}}{a}_{3}=\frac{1\cdot 0+4\cdot (-2)+3\cdot 1+1\cdot 1}{{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=-\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{3}}x \\  & =\frac{7}{4}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+\frac{11}{12}[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{12}(21[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+11[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-8[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 4 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the acute angle between $x$ and the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal.   Round the answer to $2$ decimal places.
questions.worked_solution:
Since the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{1\cdot 0+1\cdot 1+(-1)\cdot (-1)}{{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{(-1)}^{2}}{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{1\cdot 1+1\cdot 2+(-1)\cdot 2}{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{2}^{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{9}([\begin{aligned}0 \\ 9 \\ -9\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]) \\  & =\frac{1}{9}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 11 \\ -7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

 

The acute angle between $x$ and $S$ is the acute angle between $x$ and ${\text{proj}}_{S}x$ or any other non-zero vector that is parallel to ${\text{proj}}_{S}x.$ So, to make calculations easier, we can find the angle between the vectors

$\,$ $x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\,$ and $\,9\,{\text{proj}}_{S}x=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 11 \\ -7\end{aligned}].$

Computing the cosine using the dot product, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & =\frac{1\cdot 1+1\cdot 11+(-1)\cdot (-7)}{\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}}\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{11}^{2}+(-7)^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{19}{\sqrt{3}\sqrt{171}} \\  & =\frac{19}{\sqrt{3}\cdot 3\sqrt{19}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{57}}{9}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, 

$$
\theta =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{\sqrt{57}}{9})≈{32.98}^{∘},
$$

which is already an acute angle.

$$
\textrm{proj}_{S}\,\mathbf{x} 
= \textrm{proj}_{\mathbf{v}}\mathbf{x} + \textrm{proj}_{\mathbf{w}}\mathbf{x}.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $\mathbf{x}$ onto $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{v}\}$ and $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{w}\}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{\sqrt{10}\cdot 0+3\cdot 1+1\cdot 1}{{0}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}v=2[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{\sqrt{10}\cdot 0+3\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 1}{{0}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}w=(-1)[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\theta = \arccos\left( \dfrac{{\sqrt2}}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{4},
